new_steps.note: The four ifs were Stage 5; the fragile ifs were Stage 14. These are the ifs at the cliff edge: once-and-done, rather-die-than, no-point-anyway, and the ghost of a chance.

exp.what: Two points of no return. たが最後 marks the act after which the slide cannot be stopped: 彼が話し出したが最後、一時間は止まらない — once he starts talking, that's the hour gone. ばそれまでだ names the event that voids everything: 死んでしまえばそれまでだ — die, and all of it comes to nothing.
exp.build: た form + が最後 (spoken variant たら最後) + the irreversible slide. ば form + それまでだ: 忘れればそれまでだ.
exp.when: たが最後 in rueful character sketches and warnings. ばそれまでだ in memento-mori arguments — the reason to back up files, buy insurance, say the thing now.
exp.watch: たが最後 wants habitual or inevitable slides, not one-offs. ばそれまでだ's それまで is 'the end of the matter' — it pairs naturally with いくら〜ても in front: however much you save, lose the passbook and そこまで.

ex: この犬は、一度吠え出したが最後、なかなか鳴きやまない。
Once this dog starts barking, there's no stopping him.
どんな名作も、読まれなければそれまでだ。
However great the work — unread, it comes to nothing.

points.jp: 〜くらいなら・ほうがましだ

exp.what: The comparison of last resort, usually as a pair: 謝るくらいなら、死んだほうがましだ — better dead than apologizing (hyperbole with its own grammar slot). くらいなら sets the despised option; ほうがましだ names the alternative as merely LESS bad — まし never means good.
exp.build: Dictionary form + くらいなら + alternative + ほうがましだ／ほうがいい. まし stands alone too: ないよりましだ — better than nothing.
exp.when: Declarations of principle and comic despair — the pattern runs on exaggeration and everyone prices it accordingly.
exp.watch: まし is the key vocabulary item: it concedes both options are bad. 今日のほうがましだ about weather says today is less awful, not fine — mistranslating まし as 'better' loses the shrug that defines it.

ex: 満員電車に乗るくらいなら、一時間歩いたほうがましだ。
Rather walk an hour than ride that packed train.
嘘をつくくらいなら、黙っていたい。
If it comes to lying, I'd sooner say nothing.

points.jp: 〜たところで・としたって・とて
points.en: even if you did — no use

exp.what: The futility conditionals. たところで concedes the attempt and denies the payoff: 今から急いだところで、間に合わない — hurry now and you still won't make it. としたって／としたところで does the same from a supposition; とて is their classical grandparent, alive in 私とて (even I) and 今更悔やんだとて.
exp.build: た form + ところで + negative outlook. Plain form + としたって. Noun + とて (recognition-level).
exp.when: たところで in realistic pessimism — budgeting, deadlines, apologies too late. The pattern that saves wasted effort by pricing it first.
exp.watch: The ending must be negative or dismissive; a positive result flips the pattern into nonsense. Distinguish Stage 12's ても始まらない cousin: 泣いても始まらない scolds the crying; 泣いたところで無駄だ merely prices it.

ex: 今さら謝ったところで、彼女は戻らない。
Apologize now and she still isn't coming back.
私とて、好きでこの役を引き受けたわけではない。
Even I did not take this role for the pleasure of it.

points.jp: 〜ないものでもない・ないとも限らない・ではあるまいし
points.en: the ghost of a chance; it's not as if

exp.what: Three careful hedges. ないものでもない cracks a door: 考えてみないものでもない — I might just consider it (reluctance built in). ないとも限らない admits the tail risk: 事故が起きないとも限らない — one can't rule it out. ではあるまいし dismisses a comparison to scold: 子どもではあるまいし — you're not a child, so…
exp.build: ない form + ものでもない／こともない. ない form + とも限らない. Noun + ではあるまいし + the reproach (まい from Stage 12, in its fossil form).
exp.when: The first in reluctant concessions (its coyness is the message); the second in insurance logic; the third in exasperated advice between intimates.
exp.watch: ないものでもない promises almost nothing — hearing it as a yes is a genuine cross-cultural accident. ではあるまいし is scolding grammar: warm with friends, insubordinate upward.

ex: 条件次第では、引き受けないものでもない。
Depending on terms, it's not as if I'd never take it on.
初めてではあるまいし、そんなに緊張しなくてもいい。
It's not as if it's your first time — no need for those nerves.

exp.what: Two vows at opposite temperatures. てみせる stakes a demonstration: 必ず合格してみせる — I WILL pass, and you'll see it; determination performed for an audience. てやまない is the formal heart that never stops: 願ってやまない — wishing without cease; ceremonial, warm, and entirely written.
exp.build: て form + みせる for the vow (first person, future). て form + やまない with emotion verbs only: 愛して, 尊敬して, 願って.
exp.when: てみせる in sports interviews and self-talk — the comeback's grammar. てやまない in congratulatory addresses and dedications.
exp.watch: てみせる needs an audience, real or imagined — vowing it alone in a field is theater without seats, which may be the point. てやまない's verb list is short; 食べてやまない is a comedy sketch.

ex: 来年こそ、優勝してみせる。
Next year, I'll take the title — just watch.
皆様のご活躍を、心より願ってやみません。
I wish you every success, unceasingly and from the heart.

exp.what: A five-line declaration before a make-or-break attempt: the stakes (ばそれまでだ), the refused alternative (くらいなら), the priced futility of half-measures (たところで), the tail risk admitted (ないとも限らない), and the vow (てみせる).
exp.build: The order matters: stakes → refusal → realism → honesty → vow. Ending anywhere earlier is a different, sadder composition.
exp.when: The speech before the leap is a genre from job resignations to marathon starts; the machinery keeps it from being only noise.
exp.watch: One てみせる. The vow's power is its singularity — a list of vows is a to-do list.

ex: 失敗しないとも限らない。それでも、やり遂げてみせる。
It could still fail — I can't rule that out. Even so: watch me finish it.

new_steps.note: The written pivots: conceding a point before turning it, contrasting fates, singling out offenders, and reporting belief at institutional distance. rc13 closes the stage.

points.jp: 〜とはいえ・とはいうものの

exp.what: The written concession-then-turn: 春とはいえ、朝はまだ冷える — spring, granted, but the mornings still bite. The fact is accepted whole; the expectation it carries is what gets corrected. とはいうものの is the same hinge with a longer arm, often opening a paragraph against the previous one.
exp.build: Plain form／noun + とはいえ. とはいうものの sentence-initial or after a clause. Both are ものの's (Stage 12) more explicit relatives — the quote-particle と shows the concession being HELD UP first.
exp.when: Essays and reports, constantly — the polite way to disagree with a fact's implications rather than the fact. The N1 reading section's favorite hinge.
exp.watch: The turn must target the expectation, not deny the fact: 春とはいえ、まだ冬だ breaks faith with the concession. Beside けど and のに, this pair is bloodless on purpose — no frustration, just correction.

ex: 便利になったとはいえ、失ったものも多い。
Convenient it may have become — that said, much was lost.
とはいうものの、現実はそう簡単ではない。
That said, reality is not so simple.

points.en: in stark contrast; and as for the worst of them

exp.what: Two pointed contrasts. にひきかえ sets two fates side by side with a sigh built in: 兄にひきかえ、弟は… — unlike his brother, the younger one…; the comparison always shades value. に至っては descends a bad list to its floor and points: 山田に至っては、来もしなかった — and Yamada, for his part, didn't even come.
exp.build: Noun／の + にひきかえ. Noun + に至っては + the floor-level fact (often もしない for emphasis).
exp.when: にひきかえ in laments and unfavorable reviews — it is never neutral, unlike 一方. に至っては in complaints that itemize, always on the last and worst item.
exp.watch: にひきかえ between people in earshot is open invidiousness — the pattern parents are resented for. に至っては needs the list before it; as an opener it points at nothing.

ex: 去年の盛況にひきかえ、今年の客足は寂しい。
In stark contrast to last year's crowds, this year's turnout is thin.
部長に至っては、企画書を読んでさえいなかった。
And the director, for his part, hadn't even read the proposal.

points.jp: 〜ときたら・ならいざしらず
points.en: as for THAT one; if it were X, fine, but

exp.what: Two topic-markers with attitude. ときたら hauls a familiar offender onto the stand: うちの息子ときたら、ゲームばかりだ — that son of mine, honestly. ならいざしらず waives a hypothetical excuse before pressing the charge: 新人ならいざしらず、十年目の君がこのミスは — a rookie, fine, but you, in year ten?
exp.build: Noun + ときたら + the familiar exasperation. Noun + ならいざしらず（はいざしらず）+ the inexcusable case.
exp.when: ときたら in fond or genuine complaint about intimates — it cannot be formal. ならいざしらず in reprimands and self-reproach, where the waived excuse sharpens the point.
exp.watch: ときたら's target must be well-known to both speakers; a stranger ときたら baffles. ならいざしらず's hypothetical must genuinely excuse — naming a worse case (プロならいざしらず) inverts the logic.

ex: 最近の天気ときたら、まったく予報が当たらない。
This weather lately — honestly, the forecast never lands.
昔ならいざしらず、今はスマホで何でも調べられる。
In the old days, maybe — but now everything is one phone-search away.

points.jp: 〜ものと思われる・とみられる・とされる
points.en: it is believed — the institutional passive

exp.what: How institutions believe things. とみられる reports the working view: 事故原因は速度超過とみられる — excess speed is seen as the cause. ものと思われる is its fuller-dress twin; とされる cites standing consensus: 体に良いとされる — held to be healthy. Nobody in these sentences has a name — that is their function.
exp.build: Plain form + とみられる／ものと思われる／とされる. News leads on とみられる; scholarship on とされる.
exp.when: Reading the news, above all — the evening bulletin runs on this trio. Producing them in reports lends claims institutional distance, wanted or not.
exp.watch: The trio ranks by settledness: とみられる (current view) < ものと思われる (considered view) < とされる (received doctrine). Sourced claims (によると) and believed claims (とされる) are different animals — mixing them is how rumors get footnotes.

ex: 犯人は、裏口から侵入したものと思われる。
The intruder is believed to have entered by the rear door.
この温泉は、江戸時代から体に良いとされてきた。
These springs have been held salubrious since the Edo period.

points.jp: 〜ところがある・ところから・はさておき
points.en: a streak of; from which; setting aside

exp.what: Three joints for portraits and pivots. ところがある names a streak without totalizing: 彼には頑固なところがある — there's a stubborn streak in him. ところから derives a name or conclusion from a trait: よく笑うところから、福ちゃんと呼ばれる. はさておき shelves even the urgent to reach the urgent-er: 冗談はさておき — joking aside; はともかく's slightly brisker sibling.
exp.build: Adjective／clause + ところがある. Clause + ところから + naming/inference. Noun + はさておき.
exp.when: ところがある in fair-minded character sketches — kinder than flat adjectives because it leaves the rest of the person intact. ところから in etymologies and nicknames. はさておき in meetings, hourly.
exp.watch: ところがある is for tendencies, not facts — 背が高いところがある is nonsense. それはさておき is the fossil that changes subjects politely; deploy it and the room follows.

ex: 彼女には、思い込むと突っ走るところがある。
She has a streak of charging ahead once an idea takes hold.
それはさておき、本題に入りましょう。
That aside — to the matter at hand.

exp.what: N1's first stage, reviewed: minimums weighed, verdicts delivered, worth certified, cliff-edge conditions priced, and the written pivots. The through-line was EDGE — every pattern here sharpens an ordinary claim to a point.
exp.build: Doorway pairs to re-test: だに／たりとも, はおろか／もさることながら, 羽目になる／始末だ, に値する／に足る, たが最後／ばそれまでだ, とはいえ／ものの, にひきかえ／一方.
exp.when: Before the literary machine — Stage 16 assumes this stage's registers are settled furniture.
exp.watch: This stage's danger is deploying edge where none is needed: 極まりない about lukewarm tea, ときたら about a stranger. N1 grammar wrongly dosed reads as sarcasm — which natives will assume was intended.

ex: 謝罪はおろか、説明すらない始末で、憤り極まりない。
No explanation, let alone an apology — that's where it ended, and the anger is at its ceiling.
